page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU includes an L3 cache of 105 MB and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, particularly in gzip compression at 31.93 GB/sec and Geekbench single-core testing with a score of 2060.0. Multi-core performance remains in the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7912.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 7592.92. Memory bandwidth tests show 680.61 GB/sec for cached small blocks and approximately 51.52 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

The hardware profile presents specific tradeoffs. While the instance handles light LLM inference well, achieving 208.93 tokens/sec for text generation on a small 135M model, performance drops significantly to a weak 7.62 tokens/sec for text generation on a medium 7B model. This indicates a limitation for larger machine learning tasks. However, with average ratings in database operations, static web serving at 14.33 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations at 10.25 million operations per second, the instance is configured for general-purpose workloads, web serving, application hosting, and moderate database operations where extreme storage IOPS or GPU acceleration is not required.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz, it utilizes the Nitro hypervisor and includes 105 MB of L3 cache alongside support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2060.0 and strong gzip compression speeds. However, multi-core operations and larger LLM inference tasks, such as 7B model text generation, show moderate to weak performance. This resource profile makes the instance appropriate for balanced, general-purpose workloads, including web serving, application hosting, and standard database operations, offering a cost-effective balance of compute and memory without the premium of local NVMe storage.
